title: Choosing Platforms
summary: One primary platform plus optional Echo — not everywhere at once

sections.heading: Orientation — Beginning of the Lesson
sections.subtitle: Beginning of the Lesson
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **What will you understand?** **You don’t need to be everywhere**. **You need to be clear and strong** **in one place** **where people listen to you**.
- **Choosing the right platform from the start** **saves months of random experimentation** — **and makes your efforts show faster**.
bullets: **What will you understand?** **You don’t need to be everywhere**. **You need to be clear and strong** **in one place** **where people listen to you**.
**Choosing the right platform from the start** **saves months of random experimentation** — **and makes your efforts show faster**.

sections.heading: Tension — The Problem
sections.subtitle: The Problem
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Distraction among many platforms** **breaks continuity**.
- **When you post on 4 platforms** **with the same energy** — **often no platform gets its due**. **Each platform** **has a different format** **and audience behavior**.
- **The result:** **You don’t know what really worked** — **and you lose confidence** **even though the problem is in the strategy, not you**.
bullets: **When you post on 4 platforms** **with the same energy** — **often no platform gets its due**. **Each platform** **has a different format** **and audience behavior**.

sections.heading: Core Idea — One Main Platform + Simple Echo
sections.subtitle: One Main Platform + Simple Echo
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Choose one primary platform** **based on 3 factors:** **Where is your audience**, **your preferred format**, **and your ability to commit weekly**.
- **After committing for two months** **on the main platform** — **you can use an Echo Platform** **to share the same idea** **with a slight modification**.
- **Today's rule:** **The decision is not 'Where is the trend?'** — **but 'Where do I build a real relationship** **with the same people every week?'**

sections.heading: Comparison — Dispersed Thinking or Focused Thinking?
sections.subtitle: Dispersed Thinking or Focused Thinking?
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Dispersed Choice | Focused Choice |
|-------------|--------------|
| **Posting every day on a different platform** — **high fatigue and slow learning** **with no clear identity** | **Focusing on one main platform** — **a consistent publishing system** **with clearer data and steadier growth** |

sections.heading: Glossary — Important Terms
sections.subtitle: Important Terms
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| **Primary Platform** | **The platform** **where you put your best content** | **If your audience learns from short videos** — **TikTok might be the primary one** |
| **Echo Platform** | **A second platform** **where you repost your main content** **with slight modification** | **The same video idea** **after editing and changing the caption** **you post as Reels** |
| **Native Format** | **The content form** **that the platform loves and promotes** | **A strong text post on LinkedIn** **is better than a weak copied video** |

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
> **Quiz key (unchanged):** correctIndex: 0

**Question:** **You provide in-depth explanations of 8–12 minutes** **and your audience looks for details before buying** — **what do you choose as the main platform** **for the first 60 days?**

**YouTube**
Instagram Stories only****
X Threads only****

**Explanation:** **In-depth content** **needs a platform that allows for longer viewing time and full context** — **and YouTube serves this best**.
